findings.evidence: Lines 332-335 and 347-351: `linear_combination η ^ 2 * (K / (x * Q2)) * ℓ.gA * (ℓ.gA * crossSectionBracket M 0 x Q2 y H.zBosonF1 H.zBosonF2 0 - (helicitySign h * ℓ.gA - 2 * ℓ.gV) * (Yminus y * (x * H.zBosonF3))) * helicitySign_sq h`, with no comment in either proof.
findings.fix: Either prefix each `linear_combination` with a one-line comment saying the multiplier of `helicitySign_sq` eliminates the `λ²` produced by `(g_V - λ g_A)` squared/expanded, or replace the certificate with a case split: `cases h <;> simp only [helicitySign_true, helicitySign_false, ...] <;> ring`, which needs no hand-computed coefficient.
findings.issue: `gammaZTerm_eq_crossSectionBracket_sub` (line 334-335) and `zBosonTerm_eq_crossSectionBracket_sub` (line 349-351) close with an uncommented hand-computed multiplier of `helicitySign_sq h`; the zBoson one is a three-factor product containing `crossSectionBracket` itself. Nothing in the file records that the certificate exists only to substitute `λ² = 1`, so the reason the proof works is invisible and the coefficient must be recomputed by hand on any restatement.

findings.evidence: Line 288 of the same file already writes `photonTerm_eq_sq_mul_dSigmaDxDQ2 (s := 0)` and line 296 `photonTerm_eq_sq_mul_loNCdSigma (hCG := hCG)`, so the named form is available and the positional chains are gratuitous.
findings.fix: Use the named form the same file already uses: `photonTerm_eq_sq_mul_dSigmaDxDQ2 (s := helicitySign h)` and `dSigmaDxDQ2_eq_loNCdSigma (hCG := hCG)`.
findings.issue: `photonTerm_eq_sq_mul_dSigmaDxDQ2 _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (helicitySign h)` (line 229) and `dSigmaDxDQ2_eq_loNCdSigma _ _ _ _ _ _ _ hCG` (line 288) pass seven positional placeholders; adding or reordering an entry in the `variable` block at line 141 silently shifts the explicit argument into the wrong slot.

summary: Proofs are mostly short, ring/linear_combination-based and robust, but two closed-form lemmas close with hand-computed `linear_combination` certificates multiplying `helicitySign_sq` with no comment explaining why, and two applications use long positional `_` chains where the file elsewhere uses named arguments.
